issues.problem: ctx4 (keeping quiet about your own idea so the boss gets it) fits 花を持たせる (letting someone take the credit) just as well; ctx6 English 'keep face' is unidiomatic.
issues.action: Replaced ctx4 with agreeing to a one-off discount so the client's representative does not lose face; reworded ctx6 English to 'spared the president any embarrassment'.

issues.problem: ctx2 named no shameful conduct, so the milder 顔をつぶす fitted equally; ctx4 (arriving early at an interview) was far too weak an act for an idiom about serious disgrace.
issues.action: ctx2 now says the shame came from cheating in an exam; ctx4 now says the speaker works conscientiously so as not to disgrace the person who got them the job.

issues.problem: ctx3 ('you agreed until yesterday, and now you suddenly...') could be filled by 気が変わる (ky020, same set): it only showed a change of mind.
issues.action: Rewrote ctx3 so the friend turns on the speaker the moment the speaker fails, which is the self-serving reversal of attitude the idiom means.
